title: StateFlow: Enhancing LLM Task-Solving through State-Driven Workflows
abstract: StateFlow is a novel framework that models LLM workflows as state machines, allowing for better control and efficiency in task-solving. It enhances LLMs' efficiency by 13% and 28% on InterCode SQL and ALFWorld benchmarks, with 5× and 3× less cost respectively.

sections.title: The Core Insight
sections.content:
Imagine you're trying to solve a complex task, like writing a SQL query or executing a bash command. You need to follow a series of steps, and each step depends on the previous one. StateFlow is like a GPS for LLMs, guiding them through the task-solving process.

It uses a state machine to model the workflow, allowing for more precise control and adaptability.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.content:
StateFlow works by defining a set of states, each representing a distinct phase in the task-solving process. It uses a set of output functions to generate actions and transitions between states.

For example, in the SQL task, the states might include 'Init', 'Observe', 'Solve', 'Verify', and 'End'. Each state has a specific action, like executing a 'SELECT' query or verifying the output.

sections.title: Benchmark Results
sections.content:
StateFlow achieves 13% and 28% higher success rates compared to ReAct on InterCode SQL and ALFWorld benchmarks, with 5× and 3× less cost respectively.

On the InterCode SQL dataset, StateFlow outperforms ReAct by 10% in success rate, with 3× less cost.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content:
StateFlow's ability to model complex workflows and adapt to different tasks makes it a powerful tool for enhancing LLMs' efficiency.

It can be combined with iterative refining methods to further improve performance, making it a promising approach for real-world applications.

sections.title: Key Innovations
sections.content:
StateFlow's key innovation is its use of a state machine to model the task-solving process, allowing for more precise control and adaptability.

It also introduces a new way of defining output functions, which enables the model to generate actions and transitions between states.

sections.title: Try It Yourself
sections.content:
You can try StateFlow on your own tasks and datasets, using the guidelines provided in the paper.

Experiment with different state machines and output functions to see how they impact the performance of your LLM.
